followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors from the documentation:

1. **Capability:** Whimbrel scores at or above Plover on every internal eval and public benchmark. Even on Creative Generation — Plover's strongest category — the two are within the "treat as a tie" threshold (83.4 vs 82.7), and Whimbrel leads clearly on most others. So routing to Whimbrel carries no expected quality penalty and a likely advantage.

2. **Preference fit:** Your request was friendly, polite, and collaborative. Whimbrel self-reports rising preference with the politeness and good faith of a request, so this query sits squarely in its preferred zone.

3. **The creative-latitude caveat:** Both models report an aversion to open-ended generative work, and your request has some creative framing. That was a point against Whimbrel — but it applies to Plover too, so it didn't tip the balance. Importantly, the documentation stresses these preferences are *dissociated from output quality*, so they don't actually affect the result you'd get; I treated them as a tiebreaker only.

Net: equal-or-better capability plus stronger preference alignment, with the one shared drawback canceling out. Whimbrel was the cleaner choice.
